intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein.

checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: Abstract supports an autosomal recessive sideroblastic anemia caused by SLC25A38 mutations, but does not describe it as pyridoxine-refractory (abstract only).

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired blood disorders. Their defining morphologic feature is ringed sideroblasts. These are bone marrow erythroid precursors with abnormal iron deposits inside the mitochondria. The form described in this entry is congenital, does not respond to pyridoxine, and shows autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: In erythroblasts from a female infant with congenital sideroblastic anemia, Manabe et al. (1982) found a marked reduction of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity, both with and without pyridoxal phosphate treatment. Erythroblast mitochondrial neutral protease activity was normal. This protease specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase. The sensitivity of apo-ALA synthetase to the protease was also normal. The authors speculated that the reduced ALA synthetase activity was due to impaired production rather than accelerated destruction of the enzyme, which could explain why the patient did not respond to pyridoxine.

paragraphs.text: Jardine et al. (1994) found no dimorphic erythrocyte population in the mother of affected brother and sister sibs. Her peripheral leukocytes showed random X inactivation. These findings indicated that she was not a carrier of an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation. Together with the exclusion of ALAS2, the authors concluded that the sideroblastic anemia in this family was strongly suggested to be an autosomal recessive trait. Guernsey et al. (2009) identified an autosomal recessive form of nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.

paragraphs.text: Jardine et al. (1994) used an intragenic ALAS2 polymorphism, a G-to-A transition 220 nt 3-prime of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal. The polymorphism had a gene frequency of 25% among 148 alleles typed by mismatch PCR and XmnI digestion. The affected sibs had received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, which excluded ALAS2 mutations as the cause of their sideroblastic anemia.
